label: first token is one of a fixed letter/digit set (c d e f g h n o r t u w x z 0 2), plus <DEL> in length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires almost entirely at step 0 (77% of activation mass): there it is deterministic in the input token, active on every sequence whose first token is in {c,d,e,f,g,h,n,o,r,t,u,w,x,z,0,2} and never for the other 14 tokens. How strongly it fires depends on the token: e and z are strongest, n and c are near threshold. The second component is the <DEL> step of length-3 sequences. These are the largest activations (the top examples all look like xyz<DEL>), and they are strongest when the originals include l/k/v/h/i. Weaker residual firing (about 15% of mass, missed by the predicate) happens at step 3 or 4 early in longer sequences: the <DEL> step when L=4, and the step-3 original input when L>=5, almost always on a first occurrence of the token. Never fires during the copy phase (t > L) or at steps 1-2 or 5 and later.

issues: Step-0 claim checks out exactly on test: (t==0)&isin(in_tok,SET) has precision 1.000, recall 0.826 and mass recall 0.773. The complement (t==0 with a token outside the set) never fires (precision 0.0).

The L=3 <DEL> component holds up less well than the explanation suggests. Its precision is 0.81, so 19% of length-3 <DEL> steps are inactive (484 false positives on test, all at this step). The firing does not depend cleanly on whether first_tok is in the set (0.78 vs 0.85).

The residual is real and the predicate does not cover it. About 15% of activation mass sits at t=3/4: the L=4 <DEL> step fires at only a 28% rate, and step-3 originals fire at about 5-9% (slightly higher when in_tok is in SET). I could not find a clean rule for it. Conditioning on first_tok, in_first or seen(SET) gives at most about 0.21 precision, or recall under 2%. Adding L=4 <DEL> to the predicate lowers test F1 from 0.920 to 0.881.

The label leaves out the weaker t=3/4 residual, but the explanation states it openly. The other claims check out: no firing at t=1, at t>=5 or in the copy phase (t=2 has 4 hits), activation nearly always on a first occurrence (in_first=1 carries 99.7% of the mass), and the top-activating examples are all L=3 <DEL> steps.
